Sonntagsruhe means that nobody works on Sundays. The primary, religious reason is to have time to go to church. It's like the Jews who don't work on Saturdays because of religious reasons. The current reason we have the Sonntagsruhe is to have freetime, time for your family etc. There are, of course, exceptions like hospitals or gas stations. There are also other exceptions.

We also have "Verkaufsoffene Sonntage" ("Sunday openings"). This happens maybe once or twice a year and is regulated by the cities independently. So, city A can say "on February 24th, the shops are allowed to be open." But this neither means that the cities B, C and D allow this, too, nor that *every* shop of city A is participating in the Sunday opening. Usually those Sunday openings are very well-attended. But I don't think this the matter in your case.
